added.name: Index Law
added.long_description:
Index Law is building Mike-1, a superhuman AI lawyer*! Mike is an AI legal agent that gives every business the capabilities of a world-class legal team. 

Unlike traditional legal AI tools that help lawyers work faster, Mike gets legal work done directly for your business. It understands your business, reviews and negotiates contracts, handles corporate matters, and brings in vetted human lawyers when specialist expertise is needed.

Your documents, agreements, signatures, and legal history live in one workspace. Mike remembers your business and becomes more useful with every matter.

We're starting with contracts and corporate work for startups and growing businesses. Early customers have turned around contracts in under an hour and received quotes up to 80% below traditional law firm alternatives.

Our ambition is to make legal services work like software: instantly accessible, deeply personalized, and capable of handling increasingly complex work.

Try Mike: https://usemike.com

*Note: Mike-1 is an AI legal agent, not a licensed or practicing lawyer. Qualified human lawyers provide legal advice and representation where required.

added.name: Nines
added.long_description:
Nines builds autonomous robots, and the models that run them, for data centers.

The AI buildout is the biggest construction project of our lifetime, and the physical work inside it is still done by hand. Every GPU rack needs thousands of fiber connections matched, inserted, and verified before a hall goes live. After that, every building needs people on site around the clock to swap drives, transceivers, and fans.

With our robots operators bring capacity online faster, with fewer errors and less downtime.

added.name: GatherHQ
added.long_description:
Gather's AI interviews real buyers and turns what it learns into content that drives pipeline and simulations that predict customer behavior.

More than 65 enterprise marketing teams, including Envoy, Eclypsium, Cover Genius, Fortinet, CoStar, Bagel Brands, and Family Express, use Gather to continually fight AI slop and create original on-brand, third-party validated thought leadership, reports, ebooks, and campaign content.

The value of that research compounds. Every interview adds to a foundation of quantitative, qualitative, and voice data from over 300,000 real interviews across customers, with thousands added monthly. Our models use that understanding to predict how buyers will respond to messaging, pricing, and market shifts. Each answer includes supporting evidence and a confidence level. When confidence is low, Gather automatically runs new research.

Gather starts by replacing research firms and content agencies, and we aspire to build the real-time customer understanding layer that enterprises will use to drive decisions.

Built by the team that created Cooliris (acquired by Yahoo) and Pulse (acquired by Gartner), and ran Gartner Peer Insights.
added.one_liner: An API for how buyers think

added.name: Vibe Robotics
added.long_description:
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat.

Every day in every hotel, towels go up to rooms, linens move between floors, and stacks of laundry need to be folded before the next guests arrive. It’s hard, physical, and hotels can’t hire enough people to do it.

Vibe 01 is built for exactly that. It carries, delivers and folds. Two arms, a lift column, and a camera head on a base that drives itself through back-of-house hallways and service elevators. It learns by watching people do the job, then does it on its own. Vibe 01 can already fold a towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds, a skill it learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations.

We’re Archer, Daniel, Katherine and Pranav. We’re starting in hotels and building toward everywhere people work.

removed.name: InfraOptimal
removed.long_description:
We need more computers faster than we can manufacture chips, while the average GPU workload sits below 50% utilization. 

The answer is not more, it is better use of what we already have. Infraoptimal runs open models as self optimizing inference endpoints: launch any model on your own cloud or ours, and each endpoint is tuned to its model, its workload and the hardware it runs on. Behind it, our agent-driven compiler expands the search space beyond a small set of deterministically discoverable optimizations to functionally equivalent ones, proposing novel methods from state of the art literature and validating them formally, leaving reusable transformations that get better with every program they optimize. We increase speed and throughput while decreasing cost and compute.

Where Elip is going: soon your agent will look for your next job, and a company's agent will look for its next hire. Elip is where the agents meet.

long_description.before:
Foaster is building the AI-native McKinsey, starting with AI transformation.

We deploy AI agents that interview a company's employees at scale, map how work actually gets done, identify bottlenecks and AI opportunities, and draft a transformation roadmap in just 2 weeks. Expert consultants review the final outputs, add judgment where it matters, and feed their corrections back into the system.

We believe current AI models already have the capabilities required to automate most of the work consultants do. But traditional consulting firms use them to improve the old model: helping consultants work faster. 

Foaster is instead rebuilding a new model from scratch, where agents do the work that needs scale and humans review the final outputs, bring expertise, and improve the system overtime.

We are starting with AI transformation, then progressively expanding to more and more consulting projects using the same approach. Every mission creates structured knowledge from interviews, workflow maps, recommendations, and expert corrections, so the system gets better with every client engagement.

The $500B consulting market will eventually be run by our AI agents and a small number of expert humans.
long_description.after:
Foaster is building the AI infrastructure for consulting teams to run engagements with agents.

Consultants will soon direct more intelligence than any firm could ever hire. As agents take on entire workstreams, consultants will guide their work, build trust with clients, and lead change. This intelligence explosion will expand what a firm can deliver: deeper investigations, bigger problems, and entirely new types of engagements.

Foaster builds and operates the AI infrastructure behind these engagements. Our Forward Deployed Engineers configure and deploy Foaster around each firm’s methods, knowledge, and workflows, in the firm’s environment or on-premise at its clients. Once deployed, consultants run their engagements on Foaster, while our dedicated team maintains the infrastructure and advances its capabilities through applied research and benchmarking on real consulting work.

Each engagement builds a knowledge graph of the client that can be reused and extended in future work. Approved lessons strengthen the firm’s methods, while advances in models expand its capabilities. Over time, each firm builds its own intelligence layer, grounded in its expertise and the organizations it serves.

We developed this approach by running more than 20 consulting engagements ourselves during our time at Y Combinator. Using AI-led interviews at scale and autonomous process mapping, our agents investigated organizations in far greater depth than a human team could. But they could not automate the human side of an engagement: building trust, navigating difficult decisions, and leading change. So we are now bringing that technology to consulting teams.

one_liner.after: AI infrastructure for consulting teams to run engagements with agents

long_description.before:
Rodeo builds a robotic technician that automates maintenance so fleets can get vehicles back on the road sooner. Initial deployments focus on oil changes at centralized depots, where routine maintenance competes for scarce technician time.

Cofounders Michael Hazard and Colby Duke met at Applied Intuition, where they worked with OEMs like Toyota and General Motors to bring software and autonomy to vehicles. They saw firsthand how much manual work it takes to keep vehicle fleets running, and learned how to make autonomy reliable through structured testing, real-world data, and human intervention.

They’re now applying their experience to the roughly $600B annual US vehicle maintenance market. The average US vehicle is older than ever, driving up maintenance demand at a time when shops already struggle to hire and retain technicians. That gap leaves fleets facing costly downtime and preventable breakdowns.

Despite this need, vehicle maintenance has resisted traditional automation. Service information is fragmented and unreliable, and vehicle hardware varies significantly between makes and models. Rodeo builds on advances in robotic foundation models to learn maintenance skills that transfer across vehicles.

Rodeo pairs robots with human technicians who ensure each job is completed correctly, handling work the robots can’t yet perform autonomously. These deployments generate training data for Rodeo’s models through both teleoperation and hand tools augmented to record how technicians work. This lets Rodeo earn revenue while collecting the data needed to automate more of each job and improve margins.
long_description.after:

long_description.before:
Fabraix builds state-of-the-art AI red-teaming agents that continuously detect security vulnerabilities in customer-facing AI. Our product, Nyx, has already found vulnerabilities in agents at dozens of Fortune 500 companies. On AgentHarm, the leading benchmark for offensive AI security, Nyx achieved a 78% attack success rate, compared with 67% for GPT-5.6 Sol.

AI agents can change more often than teams can test them. A new model, prompt, tool, permission, or data source can change what an agent does, even when the application code stays the same. And AI is also increasing how much software companies produce and how often it changes. We built Nyx to automate the work required to red-team AI agents. It is multi modal by design and interacts with the target indirectly through controlled replicas of SaaS products and websites that we maintain, placing malicious payloads in webpages, documents, files, messages, and tool outputs to test how an agent behaves under different conditions.

Nyx often finds its first vulnerability within minutes or hours rather than days or weeks. Because the work is fully automated, companies can repeat the test with every change and at a much lower cost than what a 7-figure red-teaming (and point-in-time) engagement would require.

We're also the team behind ACE (Adversarial Cost to Exploit), a benchmark that measures AI security in terms of how much it costs attackers to break an AI system; providing a game-theoretic framework to understand how motivated a rational attacker would be in exploiting the system.

long_description.before:
Production AI agents keep making the same mistakes. The usual fix is another line in the system prompt. Over time, the agent carries instructions for dozens of situations, even when it's doing something simple, and every correction becomes another thing to maintain.

Mirrors helps developers maintain production agents by turning recurring mistakes into targeted corrections. Mirrors surfaces recurring mistakes across your production runs. You write a correction, choose the situations where it applies, and preview which past conversations it would have reached. Once activated, Mirrors adds it to your agent only in those situations. You can then compare outcomes with and without the correction to see whether it helped. Unlike skills, the agent doesn't decide what to load. The scope you set does.

Corrections live in one place, scoped to the right accounts and workflows. Mirrors connects through an SDK and works with any agent framework, and your application keeps control of its model calls and tools.

We're building Mirrors for engineering teams running customer-facing agents.

long_description.before:
Covera is the AI-native operating system for independent P&C insurance agencies. It lives inside the agency's AMS and inbox and runs agentic AI workflows across the whole client journey, from the first email to the next renewal. Producers quote first and win more business; CSRs and account managers stop retyping data.

Submissions, for producers: every new request becomes a ready file, one click keys every carrier portal for a first quote during the call, quotes come back side by side, and binding updates the AMS with no double entry.

Servicing, for CSRs and account managers: answers about any account with their source, COIs and follow-ups drafted, renewal reminders 90, 60 and 30 days out with remarketing when premiums jump, and coverage gaps across the book turned into cross-sell leads.

Agencies using Covera go from lead to quote in 5 minutes, save 10 hours a week per user and win 20% more deals against competitors. Every action is reviewed by the agency team and logged for E&O. Works with Applied Epic, AMS360, QQCatalyst, HawkSoft, EZLynx, Momentum, Gmail and Outlook.

Built by the founders of Simio (conversational AI, acquired in 2024).
long_description.after:
Insurance is one of the last big industries still running on manual work.

Trillions in premium flow through brokers who still have to key the same data into their agency management system (AMS), chase clients for documents, and fill one carrier portal after another.

Every hour spent on manual quoting is an hour not spent selling. Across tens of thousands of brokers, that's billions in revenue left on the table.

Software never fixed it, because the work sits between systems and raters are outdated.

Covera runs it end to end, with AI workflows connected to the AMS, the inbox and 100+ carrier portals. It fits the way brokers already work, so their teams can focus on advising clients and closing business.

In 3 months, Covera went live with 90+ brokers in the US and Europe. Brokers now go from a client's email to a quote in 3 minutes, instead of hours.

Covera is founded by repeat founders Tiphaine Venet and Thibaut Regerat, who previously built and sold Simio, a conversational AI company.

long_description.before: Latent catches wrong or unsupported LLM answers before they reach your users. Instead of running a second model to check every output, it reads the model's own internal state as it generates, so every request is verified with no added latency, no extra inference cost, and nothing leaving your deployment. Teams running LLMs in production, in finance, legal, healthcare and customer support, get a review queue of the answers most likely to be wrong, calibrated to their own model and traffic, with a plain explanation of why each one was flagged.
long_description.after:
Latent is a control layer for AI, built on interpretability. It reads signals inside a model as it works and checks every answer and agent action in milliseconds. Then it lets the output through, holds it, re-asks a stronger model, or sends it to review with the reason attached.

Reading the model is far cheaper than running a second LLM, so it can check every step. Latent stops 99% of rule-breaking agents before they act, against 69% for a frontier LLM judge.

It works with self-hosted and API models like GPT, Claude, and Gemini, runs hosted or in your own cloud, and calibrates to your traffic with every review.

one_liner.before: Catch wrong LLM answers before your customers do
one_liner.after: Stop AI agent mistakes by reading the model’s mind

long_description.before: Autonomous accounting platform for global companies. We close your books and give you financial clarity while you run your business.
long_description.after:
Sintropix is a financial system of record that closes your books every day and files your taxes in every country you operate in.

We connect to your banks, invoicing and payroll, and handle the accounting end-to-end. Founders get one place to do their finance work: track KPIs, see consolidated P&L and ARR reports, and forecast runway.

one_liner.before: Autonomous accounting platform for global companies
one_liner.after: AI-native ERP that closes your books and files your taxes
